question: Which editing and selection authority may an external text view own while sharing canonical document text, history and other views?
method: best-api-review/history-v2; first-principles hard-cut comparison; sequential source audit and mounted runtime probes
trigger: User explicitly requested $best-api-review audit external-text after completing documents; assessment and ledger recording only.
requirements: One canonical document owns text changes, history, schema and authored intent; mounted views own permissions, native selection and retirement.
External input engines may own local text representation, input DOM and parsing without independent persistence or undo authority.
Exact directed UTF-16 selection and patches, version validation, canonical corrections, cross-boundary navigation and plain-text transfer must preserve the current editing job.
Canonical feedback must be applied in order before a later local edit uses its observed state; stale queued predictions cannot overwrite newer accepted view state.
Review all 11 ledger units and materially different native/external, textarea, CodeMirror and authored consumers; keep other Plate features as separate scopes.
evidenceReuse: First dedicated external-text record. Reaffirms the related September 4 code review on one Text and the narrow protocol, after rereading current owners. Current local parser, composition guards and model-selection paint supersede the old implementation observations; old timing claims and the September 5 native plateau are not reused as current proof. Related native ownership reasoning remains valid. Added a mounted ordering reproduction, a protocol-only reproduction and an in-memory synchronous candidate. No upstream discovery or independent subagent review was performed.
summary: Pursue deleting deferred canonical feedback in the CodeMirror adapter: a correction followed by another same-turn canonical edit leaves displayed agoodd against canonical Ragood. Retain the public slot, versioned actions and Plite document/view ownership. A synchronous in-memory candidate passes focused tests; final sequencing and native/scale proof belong to Task design/planning.
alternatives: Keep/configure: ordinary slot and config are adequate, but extensions cannot repair the package adapter applying canonical updates out of order.

Change API: returning the canonical reply from dispatch instead of synchronous update callbacks is the strongest protocol break; the textarea already handles feedback synchronously and the candidate fixes the defect with current contracts, so a new reply channel has no demonstrated independent need.

Add primitive: reject arbitrary transaction/editor escape hatches, generic text sessions, adapter stores or another subscription owner; existing semantic actions and the shared commit fence own those jobs.

Delete/merge/inline: pursue deletion of queued canonical-update replay and dispatchingToPlite coordination in CodeMirror; inspect rejection-reset sequencing with it. Retain composition-end ordering as its distinct native job. Collapsing the adapter/view/actions types hides real directional/lifetime contracts without deleting work.

Move ownership: canonical changes/history stay in Plite, native DOM/parser stay in CodeMirror and presentation stays in copied UI. Compare synchronous feedback against publication from CodeMirror dispatchTransactions; no new runtime owner is accepted.

Replace architecture: independent CodeMirror documents/history duplicate authority; universal native or universal CodeMirror rendering each discard a current independent job. A generic DOM runtime merger still needs foreign-host, coverage and retirement mechanics.
proofLimits: 11 expected/11 reviewed/0 excluded/0 unreviewed or disposition-unresolved ledger units. Current adapter suite: 10 passed. Current product diagnostics: 1 passed/2 failed (one defect in mounted and protocol hosts). In-memory candidate plus adapter suite: 13 passed.
